scores.reason: Fixed-corpus benchmark that anchors BM25/embedding baselines against agents and disentangles retriever from agent contribution — directly answers decisions 1 and 3 (C1, C4).

GraphRAG concept-graph retrieval for generation is not citation-graph traversal in literature search; the 'graph sometimes loses to vanilla RAG' finding is analogous but would not change a decision this brief names.

Decomposes agent gains into retrieval vs utilization and shows search effort barely correlates with answer quality — mechanism-level attribution the brief's decision 2 needs, plus premise-testing evidence (C2, C5).

Shows a per-query-assembled benchmark corpus inflated agent recall from 84.3% to 21.4% once evidence moved to an independent corpus — the exact benchmark-construction and gain-failure evidence decisions 3 and 4 ask for (C4, C5).
Canonical agentic paper-search system quantifying the recall gap over single-query Google/Scholar baselines with two-benchmark construction — hits decisions 1, 2 and 3 simultaneously (C1, C2, C4).

Agentic literature-retrieval system with quantified F1 comparison against Google Scholar single-query baseline and mechanism separation (planning vs retrieval) — squarely on decisions 1 and 2, though results are on its own benchmark (C1, C2).

Shows most agent iterations add nothing and attributes recovered gains to specific control signals — informs decision 2's mechanism attribution, though on general deep-research web QA rather than literature search (C2).
Survey/taxonomy of deep-research agents with a critique of benchmark limitations; useful framing for decisions 2 and 3 but reports no measured baseline, gain, or replication itself.

Measures a concrete mechanism (search-time contamination) by which public-benchmark agent gains are inflated — the strongest kind of decision-4 evidence and exactly the premise-challenging work the brief asks the scan to reach for (C4, C5).

An agentic scientific-literature-search system whose explicit operators (citation expansion, reranking, filtering) map onto the brief's named agentic moves, with measured gains over a baseline toolset agent (C2, C3).
